chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Say, O Allah! I ask You for the words of the repentants and their deeds, and the light of the Prophets and their truthfulness, and the salvation of the Mujahideen and their reward, and the gratitude of the Chosen ones and their advice, and the deeds of the Rememberers and their conviction, and the faith of the scholars and their understanding, and the worship of the humble ones and their humility, and the wisdom of the jurists and their conduct, and the fear of the pious and their desire, and the affirmation of the believers and their reliance, and the hope of the good-doers and their righteousness.
O Allah! I ask You for the reward of the grateful, and the station of the near ones, and the companionship of the Prophets.

O Allah! I ask You for the fear of those who work for You, and the deeds of those who fear You, and the humility of those who worship You, worship You, and the conviction of those who rely upon You, and the reliance of the believers in You.

O Allah! You are Knowing of my need without being taught, and You are Capacious for it without being strained. You are the One whom no beggar exhausts, and no attainer diminishes, and no speaker's words can reach Your praise. You are as You say, and above what we say.
O Allah! Make for me a relief that is near, and a great reward, and a beautiful covering.
O Allah! You know that I am upon injustice to myself and extravagance upon it, and I have not taken for You an opposite, nor a match, nor a companion, nor a son.

O He whom questions do not confuse, O He whom nothing occupies from anything, nor hearing from hearing, nor sight from sight, and whom the insistence of the insistent does not tire. I ask You to relieve me in this hour of mine from where I expect and from where I do not expect. You revive the bones when they are dust, and You are Able over all things.

O He to whom my little gratitude did not deprive me, and my great sin did not expose me, and He saw me upon disobedience but did not confront me, and He created me for what He created me for, but I did other than what He created me for. So what a good Master You are, O my Master, and what an evil servant I am. You found me, and what a good Seeker You are, O my Lord, and what an evil sought one I am. You found me Your servant, and the son of Your servant, and the son of Your maid, before You. Do with me what You will.

O Allah! The voices have subsided, and the movements have settled, and every beloved is alone with his beloved, and I am alone with You, You are the Beloved to me. So make my solitude with You tonight the emancipation from the Fire.

O He whom no describer describes above Him, O He whom no creature has a barrier besides Him. O the First before all things, and O the Last after all things. O He who has no element, and O He whose End does not perish. O the Most Perfect of the Described, and O the Most Generous of the Givers. O He who understands every language by which He is called, and O He whose Pardoning is ancient, and His Grip is severe, and His Kingdom is upright.
I ask You by Your Name which You spoke to Musa, O Allah, O Beneficent, O Merciful, O He whom there is no god except You. O Allah! You are the Self-Sufficient.
I ask You to send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, and to admit me into Paradise by Your Mercy.
ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for all needs in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This supplication, known as *Dua al-Hajah*, is a cornerstone of Shia devotional practice, often recited for general needs (*kashifat al-karaj*). It structurally moves from invoking the spiritual stations of the righteous to affirming Allah’s absolute sufficiency (*Al-Samad*) and mercy, culminating in a humble admission of human frailty and reliance on divine grace. Scholars highlight its comprehensive nature, blending theological affirmation with practical intercession for both worldly relief and hereafter success.
